welcome.title: Assalamu alaikum
welcome.body:
This app is here to encourage prayer — to make it easy to see each prayer's time, and a small joy to mark it prayed. Everything in it is free. It will never scold you, and it will never keep asking.

A few short questions first, so the app fits you. Skip any of them.
welcome.pledge: No ads · No account · No tracking

exemption.label: Excused days
exemption.body: For the days of menstruation and post-natal bleeding, when prayer is lifted from you. Excused days are never counted as missed, never break your streak, and their prayers are not made up later — that is the agreed ruling of all the schools. Reminders pause while they last, and you can choose to keep hearing the adhan. Illness and travel are different: those prayers are still owed, so log those days as usual. (Ramadan fasts are made up as well, but fasting is beyond this app.)

pledge.title: No ads, ever

points.ads: No ads. Not now, not later.

points.device: Your prayer log stays on this phone — unless you add a buddy, and then each prayer you mark is sent to their phone.

pledge.footnote: Four things can ever leave this phone. The city lookup — a city name you type, or your approximate position when you use your device's location; your phone asks its own map service, and neither ever reaches us. Anonymous crash reporting — whether the app crashed or ran cleanly, never who you are or what you did — which you can switch off here in Settings. A tip, if you ever leave one, which goes through the App Store or Google Play like any purchase. And, only if you add a buddy, the prayers you mark — one flag each, carried to their phone by a relay of ours that deletes it as soon as their phone has it, and holds no name, no location and no record of you.
pledge.footnoteWithoutCrashReports: Three things can ever leave this phone. The city lookup — a city name you type, or your approximate position when you use your device's location; your phone asks its own map service, and neither ever reaches us. A tip, if you ever leave one, which goes through the App Store or Google Play like any purchase. And, only if you add a buddy, the prayers you mark — one flag each, carried to their phone by a relay of ours that deletes it as soon as their phone has it, and holds no name, no location and no record of you.

diagnostics.body: If the app crashes, it sends an anonymous report of where the code failed so the bug can be fixed — never your prayer log, your location, or anything that says who you are. Turning this off takes effect the next time you open the app.

inexact.footnote: The button opens a screen on your phone. Turn on “Alarms & reminders” there, then come back.

battery.title: Battery settings can stop reminders
battery.body: Android pauses apps it thinks you are not using, which can stop a scheduled adhan from arriving. Exempting this app from battery optimisation prevents that.
battery.bodyOem: {{brand}} phones pause background apps more aggressively than most, which can stop a scheduled adhan from arriving. Exempting this app from battery optimisation, and letting it start on its own, prevents that.
battery.bodyXiaomi: {{brand}} phones pause background apps more than most, and a paused app cannot deliver the adhan. These phones keep their own setting for it: open Settings, then Apps, then Simple Prayer, then Battery saver, and choose No restrictions. It also helps to open your recent apps and lock Simple Prayer there, so the phone does not close it.
battery.cannotCheck: The app cannot read this setting from the inside, so it cannot tell you whether the exemption is already in place. The screen it opens can.
battery.exempt: Android’s own battery limits are already switched off for this app. Your phone maker can have a separate setting of its own, which the app cannot read.
battery.restricted: Android’s battery limits are still on for this app, so a reminder can be held back or dropped. The button below opens the screen that changes it.

organizer.title: Android may sort reminders into a group
organizer.body: Newer Android phones can sort notifications into groups such as Promotions or Suggested. A reminder placed in one of those groups arrives without a sound. You can tell your phone to leave this app out.
organizer.cannotCheck: The app cannot see this from the inside, so it cannot tell you whether your phone is doing it. On the screen the button opens, look for Notification organizer, then the list of apps to leave out.

available.title: Reminders while the app is closed
available.body: The app sets reminders a few days ahead. It adds more days when the phone gives it a moment in the background. Without those moments the reminders run out.
available.cannotCheck: The app cannot read this setting from the inside. The button opens this app's page in Settings. The switch there is called Background App Refresh. There is one for all apps under Settings, then General.

restricted.title: The phone is not giving the app background time
restricted.body: Reminders that are already set will still arrive. The app cannot add new days while it is closed, so they run out after a few days. Opening the app tops them up again.

ios.title: If a reminder arrives silently
ios.body: Focus and Do Not Disturb silence notifications while they are on, and Scheduled Summary holds them back until later. Letting this app through is done in the system settings.

reminderHealth.pledge: This app schedules several days of reminders ahead and rebuilds them every time you open it. You never have to open it just to keep the adhan working.
